en.title: Substring with the Highest Prefix and Suffix Match Score
en.description:
Choose a non-empty substring t of text. The prefix score is the longest length by which a prefix of t matches a suffix of prefixString; the suffix score is the longest length by which a suffix of t matches a prefix of suffixString. The total score is their sum, and the two matches may overlap; on a tie for the highest score, choose the lexicographically smallest t.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site; missing numeric bounds and recoveries of source typos are all stated explicitly.
en.input: Three lines: text, prefixString, and suffixString, in that order; complete OCR bounds: each has length 1..50 and contains only lowercase letters; text is guaranteed to match at least one character on at least one side.
en.output: Output the lexicographically smallest non-empty substring with the highest score.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: engin; banana; a. These answers were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Enumerate all non-empty candidate substrings; for each side, enumerate match lengths not exceeding the candidate's length, then find the maximum score and compare lexicographically.
